BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Fresh and older wind slabs are to be assessed with care and prudence.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
The sometimes strong wind has transported the new snow significantly. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls the wind slabs have increased in size additionally. Above approximately 2300 m the avalanches can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers and reach large size.
New snow and wind slabs can in some cases be released by a single winter sport participant. This applies in particular on very steep slopes at intermediate and high altitudes.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
BulletinMeasurements.snowpackStructureComment: 30 to 40 cm of snow fell in the last few days above approximately 1500 m. The sometimes moderate wind has transported the new snow. Faceted weak layers exist in the snowpack in particular in places that are protected from the wind, especially in the Prealps.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Weak layers in the old snowpack necessitate caution. Fresh wind slabs require caution.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
Weak layers in the lower part of the snowpack can be released by winter sport participants. This applies on steep west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Remotely triggered avalanches are possible in isolated cases. This applies in high Alpine regions. Mostly the avalanches are medium-sized.
In addition the fresh wind slabs should be taken into account. Such avalanche prone locations are to be found in steep terrain above approximately 2400 m. Caution is to be exercised adjacent to ridgelines, as well as in gullies and bowls, and behind abrupt changes in the terrain. The number and size of avalanche prone locations will increase with altitude. Avalanches can reach medium size.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
BulletinMeasurements.snowpackStructureComment:
Avalanche prone weak layers exist in the old snowpack. This applies in particular on west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Whumpfing sounds and the formation of shooting cracks when stepping on the snowpack and fresh avalanches serve as an alarm indicating the danger.

Over a wide area 15 to 20 cm of snow, and up to 30 cm in some localities, fell on Thursday. The wind has transported the new snow. This applies in particular at high altitudes and in high Alpine regions. The fresh wind slabs are lying on soft layers.
BulletinMeasurements.tendencyComment: The avalanche danger will persist. Experience in the assessment of avalanche danger is required.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Wind slabs require caution. Slab avalanches are possible.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
On wind-loaded slopes and on extremely steep slopes dry avalanches are possible, even medium-sized ones. Above approximately 2300 m they can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers. As the day progresses the likelihood of dry and moist snow slides being released will increase in particular on very steep sunny slopes. Gliding avalanches can also occur, in particular on steep grassy slopes. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided.
Wind slabs can in some cases be released by a single winter sport participant. They represent the main danger, especially on very steep slopes. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls and behind abrupt changes in the terrain the likelihood of avalanches is higher.
BulletinMeasurements.snowpackStructureComment:
In particular in the northwest 15 to 30 cm of snow fell in the last two days above approximately 1300 m.
As a consequence of the occasionally strong northerly wind, the snow drift accumulations have increased in size at the weekend.
Above approximately 2200 m there are 70 to 140 cm of snow, and even as much as 190 cm in some localities, especially above approximately 2500 m.
During the sunny day, the surface snow becomes moist below 2300 m. In some places, where the wind has had a greater effect, it has a chalky consistency.
It is not distinctly layered. Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.
BulletinMeasurements.tendencyComment: The weather conditions will facilitate a gradual strengthening of the snowpack. The danger will decrease gradually.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Wind slabs represent the main danger.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
The sometimes strong wind has transported the new snow significantly. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls the wind slabs have increased in size additionally. In particular here medium-sized and, in isolated cases, large avalanches are possible.
In addition the soft wind slabs above the tree line are easily triggered.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

Faceted weak layers exist in the snowpack in particular in places that are protected from the wind. Below approximately 2000 m from a snow sport perspective, in most cases insufficient snow is lying.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Wind slabs at intermediate and high altitudes. Slab avalanches are possible.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
The sometimes strong wind has transported the new snow. In particular adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls small and, in isolated cases, medium-sized slab avalanches are possible. In addition the soft wind slabs are capable of being triggered.
In particular on very steep sunny slopes and in steep rocky terrain small and medium-sized dry and moist avalanches are possible as a consequence of solar radiation.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

The solar radiation will give rise as the day progresses to moistening of the snowpack in particular at low and intermediate altitudes.

In particular on very steep sunny slopes and in steep rocky terrain mostly small dry and moist avalanches are possible as a consequence of solar radiation. Individual gliding avalanches can also occur.

Towards its base, the snowpack is faceted and weak.

Avalanches can reach medium size.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Individual avalanche prone locations are to be found on wind-loaded slopes at intermediate and high altitudes.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment: The avalanche prone locations are very rare. They are to be found on extremely steep shady slopes in high Alpine regions and on wind-loaded slopes. As a consequence of solar radiation individual small natural moist avalanches are possible. Restraint should be exercised because avalanches can sweep people along and give rise to falls. The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.
BulletinMeasurements.snowpackStructureComment: 15 to 30 cm of snow fell in the last few days above approximately 1600 m. The moderate wind has transported some snow. The new snow is loosely bonded on wind-protected shady slopes. As a consequence of solar radiation a crust will form on the surface.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment: Avalanches can scarcely be released, but they will be small in most cases, in particular on very steep shady slopes at elevated altitudes.
